properties.name: SA-REKS ensemble energy and configuration energies
properties.brief: Weighted sum of the energies E_{X} of the SA-pool configurations, with the weights w_{X} of `SA_REKS_WEIGHTS`.
properties.variables: `SCF TOTAL ENERGY`, `CURRENT REFERENCE ENERGY`, `CURRENT ENERGY` (§si_reks_grad), `REKS SA_WEIGHTS`, `REKS W_PPS`, `NUCLEAR REPULSION ENERGY`, `ONE-ELECTRON ENERGY`, `TWO-ELECTRON ENERGY`, `DFT XC ENERGY`
bullets: The configuration energies E_{X} are printed, not stored.
`Total Energy` of `Energetics` equals `@REKS Final Energy` and the `Total energy` row of the decomposition; without an IPR penalty it equals `E[SA-REKS]`.
With `REKS_DELOC_IPR_PENALTY` > 0 both blocks add a penalty row, and `Total energy` = `E[SA-REKS]` + `IPR penalty energy` (§reks_deloc_ipr_penalty).

properties.name: Fractional occupation numbers of the SA-REKS ensemble
properties.brief: FONs n_{p}, n_{q} (n_{p} + n_{q} = 2) of the active orbitals of each geminal (p,q), one set per FON generation (§4).
properties.for: every generation with at least one active geminal in the SA ensemble
properties.variables: `REKS FON`, `REKS <L>_FON` (L = M, U, V, W, X, Y, Z), `REKS FON META`, `REKS <L>_FON META`; `REKS N ACTIVE ELECTRONS`, `REKS N ACTIVE ORBITALS`, `REKS G`, `REKS N SECTORS`
properties.files: `<prefix>.molden` (`MOLDEN_WRITE`): `Occup` of the active MOs = FONs of set n, not natural occupations
bullets: FON arrays: (u − 1) × n_{g}, u = widest geminal width, n_{g} = geminals of the generation; row r = free FON n_{r}, the last FON is 2 − Σ; unused cells −1. META arrays: (1 + u) × n_{g}, pairing scheme (row 0) and MO indices (rows 1..).
Check: the MOs of `Pairing scheme 0` equal `Active MO indices` of the setup (§diag-wrong-window); `2.000000`/`0.000000` lie at the bound (§diag-fon-pinned).

properties.name: GVB-DIIS convergence quality
properties.brief: Diagnostics of the finished GVB-DIIS run: final orbital-gradient norms, landings, verdict trips, highest fallback rung (0 ARMED, 1 RETAIN, 2 FALLBACK), basin fires, and GRAZING = 1 when the final iterate landed within a decade of a convergence gate (CLEAN otherwise).
properties.variables: `REKS QUALITY GORB FRO`, `REKS QUALITY GORB RMS`, `REKS QUALITY LANDINGS`, `REKS QUALITY VERDICT TRIPS`, `REKS QUALITY MAX RUNG`, `REKS QUALITY BASIN FIRES`, `REKS QUALITY GRAZING`; `REKS GORB FRO`, `REKS GATE RMS`; `SCF ITERATIONS`
bullets: Printed only at `REKS_REPORT_LEVEL` ≥ 4, as one `[QUALITY]` trace line.
`REKS GORB FRO` and `REKS GATE RMS` hold the value of the last SCF iteration that set them (TRAH after iteration 0; GVB-DIIS with a nonzero orbital gradient, the witnessed gradient norm).

properties.name: FONs of the SI-only geminals
properties.brief: FONs of geminals that enter only SI configurations, optimized after the SCF at fixed SA-REKS orbitals (§2).
properties.for: SI configurations with geminals absent from the SA ensemble
properties.variables: `REKS FON K=<e>`, `REKS <L>_FON K=<e>`, `REKS FON META K=<e>`, `REKS <L>_FON META K=<e>` (sector form `REKS SECTOR <s> …`); per SI cassette, per generation whose FON layer holds all geminals of the cassette
bullets: No bare (cassette 0) alias.
Read the `Residual` column. Geminals without `*` printed as `2.000000/0.000000` lie at the bound, as scheme 1 `(a,c)` above; compare the same columns between runs.

properties.name: SSR state energies
properties.brief: Eigenvalues of the SI eigenproblem of each cassette after removal of the overlap null modes (§2); states ordered by energy, root index 0-based.
properties.for: every physical root of every SI cassette with at least one configuration, independent of `SI_REKS_STORE_STATES` and `SI_REKS_PRINT_STATES`
properties.units: E_{h} (stored); E_{h} and eV relative to the lowest state of the first typed SI cassette, S0 when that cassette is a singlet (printed)
properties.variables: `SSR ENERGIES K=<e>`; bookkeeping `SSR SI LIST`, `SSR CASSETTE 2S K=<e>`, `SSR STORED STATES K=<e>`, `SSR ACTIVE ORBITALS K=<e>`, `SSR CASSETTE SECTOR K=<e>`
bullets: The four bookkeeping scalars never take the sector prefix.
`Adiabatic states` lists `SI_REKS_PRINT_STATES` rows; in later cassettes a `ref` row repeats S0 of cassette 0.
`State summary`, printed with two or more SI cassettes, merges the printed states of the first cassette of each multiplicity by energy.

Check E(S0) against `@REKS Final Energy` (`E[SA-REKS]`) and the gaps between neighbouring roots: in the runs of this manual E(S0) lies 0.04–0.48 E_{h} below E_{SA}; S0 = −1.0·10^{7} E_{h} at E_{SA} = −1.27 E_{h} marks ghost states (§diag-ghost-states).

properties.name: SSR eigenvectors and Chirgwin–Coulson weights
properties.brief: Eigenvector c of each state over the configurations of its cassette, and the Chirgwin–Coulson weights ω_{j} (§2), printed in `Adiabatic states` (§ssr-energies).
properties.variables: `SSR COEFFICIENTS K=<e>` (`REKS_REPORT_LEVEL` ≥ 3)
bullets: The weights are printed, not stored.
No bare (cassette 0) alias.

properties.name: SI Hamiltonian and overlap
properties.brief: Hamiltonian H and overlap S of the cassette over its configurations, before diagonalization; the printed block gives dimensions, the number of overlapping pairs and the rank after Löwdin regularization.
formulas: V_{ij} = \tilde H_{ij} - \tilde S_{ij}\,\frac{\tilde H_{ii} + \tilde H_{jj}}{2}, \qquad \tilde S_{ij} = \frac{S_{ij}}{\sqrt{S_{ii} S_{jj}}}, \quad \tilde H_{ij} = \frac{H_{ij}}{\sqrt{S_{ii} S_{jj}}}
properties.variables: `SSR HAMILTONIAN K=<e>`, `SSR OVERLAP SPARSE K=<e>` (rows [i n_{cfg} + j, S_{ij}]), stored at `REKS_REPORT_LEVEL` ≥ 3
bullets: Matrices printed only at `REKS_REPORT_LEVEL` ≥ 4. No bare (cassette 0) alias.

`Independent states` = `Configurations` − overlap null modes − ghost states. A `Regularization` line appears when null modes are removed, a `Ghost states` line when roots more than 100 E_{h} above the lowest are removed (§diag-ghost-states).
Two configurations with |S̃_{ij}| close to 1 are nearly the same function; their coupling then follows from the overlap, and V_{ij} vanishes for two identical functions.

The `Consistency` line (second fragment, H_{4} REKS(4,4)) gives the largest |V_{ij}| in mE_{h} over the pairs with |S̃_{ij}| > 0.99 (a fixed bound, not an option) and the pair where it occurs; without such a pair the line is absent. The code sets no bound on |V_{ij}|.

properties.name: Orbitals of the SI step
properties.brief: MO coefficients of the SI state-property evaluation (the Fock-snapshot orbitals when present, else the SCF orbitals; the basis of the Dyson MO arrays) and the number of core orbitals.
properties.variables: `REKS C PATH B K=<e>`, `REKS NCORE K=<e>`
bullets: Sector form drops the leading `REKS `: `REKS SECTOR <s> C PATH B K=<e>`.

properties.name: Transition dipole moments and length-form oscillator strengths
properties.brief: Transition dipoles between adiabatic states from the unrelaxed transition densities, and the length-form oscillator strengths.
properties.for: pairs I < J
properties.units: e a_{0} (stored); e a_{0} and D (printed); f dimensionless
formulas: f_{\mathrm{len}} = \tfrac{2}{3}\,\Delta E\,|\boldsymbol\mu_{IJ}|^2 \quad (\Delta E \text{ in } E_{\mathrm h})
properties.variables: `SSR TRANSITION DIPOLES K=<e>`, `SSR OSCILLATOR STRENGTHS K=<e>`
bullets: The `*` flag after f_{len} (length and velocity forms differ by more than a factor of 3, tested when f_{len} or f_{vel} exceeds 10^{-3}) appears only when the velocity table is computed too (`E_TDM_VEL` or `M_TDM`).
λ prints `-` for a gap that prints as 0.000 eV.

properties.name: Velocity-form transition moments and oscillator strengths
properties.brief: Velocity-form transition moments and oscillator strengths, printed with the magnetic moments (§transition-magnetic).
properties.for: pairs I < J
properties.variables: `SSR VELOCITY TRANSITION DIPOLES K=<e>`, `SSR OSCILLATOR STRENGTHS VELOCITY K=<e>`
bullets: `*` after f_{vel}: same test as after f_{len} (§transition-dipole).
The NAC sum-rule check against −p (§nac) is printed only when these moments exist.

properties.name: Magnetic transition moments and rotatory strengths
properties.brief: Magnetic transition moments and velocity-form rotatory strengths, printed in the velocity table (§transition-velocity).
properties.for: pairs I < J; `M_TDM` also computes the transition dipoles
formulas: \boldsymbol\mu_{IJ} = -\langle I|\mathbf r|J\rangle, \qquad \mathbf p_{IJ} = \langle I|\nabla|J\rangle, \qquad \mathbf m_{IJ} = -\tfrac12\,\langle I|\mathbf r\times\nabla|J\rangle, \qquad R_{\mathrm{len}} = \boldsymbol\mu_{IJ}\cdot\mathbf m_{IJ}, \qquad R_{\mathrm{vel}} = -\frac{\mathbf p_{IJ}\cdot\mathbf m_{IJ}}{\Delta E}
properties.variables: `SSR MAGNETIC TRANSITION DIPOLES K=<e>`, `SSR ROTATORY STRENGTHS K=<e>` (columns [R_{len}, R_{vel}])
bullets: μ includes the electron charge −1; m is real (the factor i of the operator is dropped).
R_{len} is stored, not printed; the table prints R_{vel}.

properties.name: Natural orbitals and occupations of the active space
properties.brief: Eigenvectors and eigenvalues of the active 1-RDM of each state; orbitals expanded over the active MOs.
properties.variables: `SSR NATURAL OCCUPATIONS K=<e>`, `SSR NATURAL ORBITALS ACTIVE STATE=<k> K=<e>`, `SSR NATURAL ORBITALS AO STATE=<k> K=<e>`
bullets: Stored occupations are in descending order (NO 1 = largest); the printed rows follow the active MOs, each NO on the row of its dominant MO coefficient, and the occ header follows that row order.
The occupations of each state sum to the number of active electrons.

properties.name: Radical character
properties.brief: Indices y_{0}, y_{1} (occupations of the LUNO and LUNO+1) and the effective numbers of unpaired electrons, over the active natural occupations n_{a} of the state (descending).
properties.variables: `SSR RADICAL INDICES K=<e>` (columns [y0, y1, N_D, N_U, N_U,nl]), `SSR UNPAIRED ATOMIC POPULATIONS K=<e>`
bullets: Unpaired atomic populations are stored, not printed.
y_{0}, y_{1} equal the corresponding occupations in `Natural orbitals` (§natural-orbitals); they are not Yamaguchi's spin-projected index. `-` is printed when the active space has no LUNO or LUNO+1.
properties.ref: N_{D}: Takatsuka–Fueno–Yamaguchi; N_{U} (linear) and N_{U,nl} (nonlinear): Head-Gordon 2003 (§16).

properties.name: Permanent and difference dipole moments (unrelaxed)
properties.brief: Dipole moment of each state from the unrelaxed state density, origin 0, and the difference dipole relative to S0.
properties.for: difference dipoles: two or more states
properties.units: e a_{0} (stored); e a_{0} and D (printed)
properties.variables: `SSR PERMANENT DIPOLES K=<e>`, `SSR DIFFERENCE DIPOLES K=<e>`

properties.name: Quadrupole moments of the states (unrelaxed)
properties.brief: Full Cartesian quadrupole of each state (nuclei and electrons, origin 0) from the unrelaxed state density, and its traceless part.
properties.variables: `SSR QUADRUPOLES K=<e>`, `SSR TRACELESS QUADRUPOLES K=<e>`
bullets: Components xx, xy, xz, yy, yz, zz.

properties.name: Transition second moments
properties.brief: Cartesian second moments of the transition density of each pair, trace included.
properties.for: pairs I < J
formulas: \langle I|\textstyle -\sum r_i r_j|J\rangle, \qquad i, j = x, y, z
properties.variables: `SSR TRANSITION QUADRUPOLES K=<e>`

properties.name: Cartesian multipole moments of order l ≥ 3
properties.brief: Cartesian multipole moments of order l of each state (nuclei included) and of each transition; components x^{a} y^{b} z^{c}, a + b + c = l, in lexicographic order, origin 0, trace included.
properties.for: one table per order l = 3..n
formulas: M_I = \sum_A Z_A\, x_A^a y_A^b z_A^c - \langle I|\textstyle\sum_i x_i^a y_i^b z_i^c|I\rangle
properties.variables: `SSR MULTIPOLES L=<l> K=<e>`, `SSR TRANSITION MULTIPOLES L=<l> K=<e>`

properties.name: Atomic charges of the states (unrelaxed)
properties.brief: Mulliken and Löwdin charges of each state from the spin-summed unrelaxed state density P^{(I)} = D^{c} + C_{a} ρ^{(II)} C_{a}^{T} (core D^{c} included).
formulas: q^{\mathrm M}_A = Z_A - \sum_{\mu\in A}(\mathbf P^{(I)}\mathbf S)_{\mu\mu}, \qquad q^{\mathrm L}_A = Z_A - \sum_{\mu\in A}(\mathbf S^{1/2}\mathbf P^{(I)}\mathbf S^{1/2})_{\mu\mu}
properties.variables: `SSR MULLIKEN CHARGES K=<e>`, `SSR LOWDIN CHARGES K=<e>`
bullets: Change tables X(S_{j}) − X(S_{i}) print entries with |change| ≥ `SI_REKS_ANALYSIS_CHANGE_MIN` (default 0.1); rows and tables without such a change are omitted.
The charges of each state sum to the molecular charge.

properties.name: Transition charges
properties.brief: Mulliken and Löwdin atomic charges of the transition density ρ^{(IJ)} of each pair I → J: the formulas of §atomic-charges with P^{(I)} replaced by C_{a} ρ^{(IJ)} C_{a}^{T}, without Z_{A}; the charges of a pair sum to 0.
properties.for: pairs I < J
properties.variables: `SSR TRANSITION MULLIKEN CHARGES K=<e>`, `SSR TRANSITION LOWDIN CHARGES K=<e>`

properties.name: Bond indices of the states (unrelaxed)
properties.brief: Mayer and Wiberg–Löwdin bond indices of each atom pair A ≠ B from the spin-summed unrelaxed state density P^{(I)} (§atomic-charges).
properties.for: printed rows: pairs with index ≥ 0.10 in any state; change tables as for the charges (§atomic-charges)
properties.variables: `SSR MAYER INDICES K=<e>`, `SSR WIBERG LOWDIN INDICES K=<e>` (m × natom^{2}, column A·natom + B)
bullets: No spin-density term: for open-shell states this is not the open-shell Mayer index.

properties.name: Natural transition orbitals
properties.brief: Hole/particle orbital pairs of the transition density T_{pq} with weights w_{k}, the participation ratio PR, and the magnitude Ω of the transition density.
properties.for: pairs I < J
formulas: \mathbf T = \boldsymbol\rho^{(IJ)} = \mathbf U\,\mathrm{diag}(s_k)\,\mathbf V^{\mathsf T}, \qquad w_k = \frac{s_k^2}{\sum_l s_l^2}, \qquad \mathrm{PR} = \Big(\sum_k w_k^2\Big)^{-1}
properties.variables: `SSR NTO WEIGHTS K=<e>`, `SSR NTO HOLES AO ROOT <I> -> ROOT <J> K=<e>`, `SSR NTO PARTICLES AO ROOT <I> -> ROOT <J> K=<e>`
properties.files: `<prefix>.nto.<label I>-<label J>_cassette<e>.molden` (`MOLDEN_WRITE`, stored states above 0); cube `CUBEPROP_TASKS` `SSR_NTOS` (pairs with w ≥ 0.1)
bullets: Holes: columns of U, particles: columns of V (active MOs; AO form C_{a}U, C_{a}V). T is spin-summed, so a pure singlet single excitation has Ω = 1. The first three weights are printed; weights and PR print `-` when Ω < 0.05.
The bare alias of `SSR NTO HOLES`/`PARTICLES` exists only for pairs 0 → J of cassette 0; `SSR NTO WEIGHTS` has the full bare alias.

properties.name: Exciton descriptors, hole and electron populations, natural difference orbitals
properties.brief: Descriptors of the transition density (d_{h→e}, σ_{h}, σ_{e}, d_{exc}, R_{eh}, p_{prom}), Löwdin hole and electron populations per atom, and the eigenpairs of the difference density ρ^{(JJ)} − ρ^{(II)}.
properties.for: pairs I < J
properties.units: distances a_{0}; R_{eh} dimensionless; populations and p_{prom} electrons
formulas: \Omega_{AB} = \tfrac12\sum_{\mu\in A}\sum_{\nu\in B}\big[(\mathbf X\mathbf T\mathbf X^{\mathsf T})_{\mu\nu}\big]^2, \quad \mathbf X = \mathbf S^{1/2}\mathbf C_a, \qquad h_A = \sum_B \Omega_{AB}, \quad e_B = \sum_A \Omega_{AB}

\langle \mathbf r\rangle_h = \frac{\mathrm{tr}(\mathbf T^{\mathsf T}\mathbf r\,\mathbf T)}{2\Omega}, \quad \langle \mathbf r\rangle_e = \frac{\mathrm{tr}(\mathbf T\,\mathbf r\,\mathbf T^{\mathsf T})}{2\Omega}, \quad \langle r^2\rangle_h = \frac{\mathrm{tr}(\mathbf T^{\mathsf T}\mathbf r^2\,\mathbf T)}{2\Omega}, \quad \langle \mathbf r_h\cdot\mathbf r_e\rangle = \frac{\sum_a \mathrm{tr}(\mathbf T^{\mathsf T} \mathbf x_a \mathbf T \mathbf x_a)}{2\Omega}

d_{h\to e} = |\langle\mathbf r\rangle_e - \langle\mathbf r\rangle_h|, \qquad \sigma_{h} = \sqrt{\langle r^2\rangle_{h} - |\langle\mathbf r\rangle_{h}|^2}, \qquad \sigma_{e} = \sqrt{\langle r^2\rangle_{e} - |\langle\mathbf r\rangle_{e}|^2}

d_{\mathrm{exc}} = \sqrt{\langle r^2\rangle_h + \langle r^2\rangle_e - 2\langle\mathbf r_h\cdot\mathbf r_e\rangle}, \qquad R_{eh} = \frac{\langle\mathbf r_h\cdot\mathbf r_e\rangle - \langle\mathbf r\rangle_h\cdot\langle\mathbf r\rangle_e}{\sigma_h\sigma_e}
properties.variables: `SSR EXCITON DESCRIPTORS K=<e>` (columns [Ω, d_{h→e}, σ_{h}, σ_{e}, d_{exc}, R_{eh}, p]), `SSR DIFFERENCE DENSITY EIGENVALUES K=<e>`, `SSR CT OMEGA ATOMS K=<e>`, `SSR EXCITON HOLE POPULATIONS K=<e>`, `SSR EXCITON PARTICLE POPULATIONS K=<e>`, `SSR NDO AO ROOT <I> -> ROOT <J> K=<e>`
properties.files: `<prefix>.ndo.<label I>-<label J>_cassette<e>.molden` (`MOLDEN_WRITE`, stored states above 0); cube `CUBEPROP_TASKS` `SSR_NDOS` (|λ| ≥ 0.1), `SSR_ATTACHMENT_DETACHMENT`
bullets: `-` in the d_{h→e} … R_{eh} columns = Ω below 0.05 (or a zero transition density); p_{prom} is printed for every pair.

x_{a}, r and r^{2} are the AO dipole and second-moment integrals in the active MO basis; Ω_{AB} is the Löwdin form, not the Mulliken-type Ω of Plasser–Lischka. h_{A}, e_{B} are not normalized; each sums to Ω. NDOs are C_{a} v_{k}.
`SSR CT OMEGA ATOMS`, the hole/particle populations and `SSR NDO AO` have no bare (cassette 0) alias.

properties.name: Fragment charge-transfer descriptors
properties.brief: Charge moved between fragments, TheoDORE CT number (h/e split), participation ratios PR_{i}, PR_{f}, PR_{F}, DEL, localization POS, and Löwdin hole and electron populations per fragment.
properties.for: a molecule of at least 2 fragments (`--` separators), no ghost fragments or atoms; pairs I < J
properties.units: q_{moved}, ΔN_{F} in e; other columns dimensionless
formulas: \Delta N_F = N^{\mathrm L}_F(J) - N^{\mathrm L}_F(I), \qquad q_{\mathrm{moved}} = \sum_F \max(0, \Delta N_F)
properties.variables: `SSR CT FRAGMENT DESCRIPTORS K=<e>` (columns [CT, PRi, PRf, PR, DEL, POS]), `SSR CT FRAGMENT HOLE POPULATIONS K=<e>`, `SSR CT FRAGMENT PARTICLE POPULATIONS K=<e>`
bullets: q_{moved} and Net ΔN_{F} are printed, not stored; stored column CT is the printed h/e split. The fragment populations have no bare (cassette 0) alias.

Ω_{FG} sums the atom-pair Ω_{AB} of §exciton over the fragments; F in POS is 1-based; N^{L}_{F} is the Löwdin active population of fragment F. Printed headers: `h/e split` for CT, `PR_F` for PR. CT to POS print `-` when Ω < 0.05; q_{moved} is always printed.
The fragment line (`F1 = atoms 1-3, F2 = atoms 4-6`) shows the partition used.

properties.name: Fragment couplings (FCD, FED)
properties.brief: Diabatic coupling V_{F} between fragments F and G: FCD from the charge difference D = q(F) − q(G) (Löwdin and Mulliken charges), FED from the excitation difference D = x(F) − x(G) between excited states.
properties.for: a molecule of at least 2 fragments (`--` separators), no ghost fragments or atoms; FED needs at least 2 excited states; printed: pairs with |D_{I} − D_{J}| ≥ 0.1
formulas: \text{FCD:}\ D_{mn} = q^F_{mn} - q^G_{mn}, \quad q^F_{mm} = \sum_{A\in F} q_A(m), \quad q^F_{mn} = \sum_{A\in F} q_A(m\to n)

\text{FED:}\ D_{mn} = x^F_{mn} - x^G_{mn}, \quad x^F_{mn} = \tfrac12\,\mathrm{tr}\big[\mathbf T_m^{\mathsf T}(\mathbf G^F\mathbf T_n + \mathbf T_n\mathbf G^F)\big], \quad \mathbf T_m = \boldsymbol\rho^{(0m)}, \quad m, n \ge 1
properties.variables: `SSR FCD LOWDIN COUPLINGS <F> <G> K=<e>`, `SSR FCD MULLIKEN COUPLINGS <F> <G> K=<e>`, `SSR FED COUPLINGS <F> <G> K=<e>`
bullets: States m < n of one cassette, fragments F < G; q_{A} are the state and transition charges (§atomic-charges, §transition-charges), G^{F} the Löwdin projector on the atoms of F. V carries the sign of D_{mn}, which follows the state phases; compare |V| with literature values. `*` marks a row where the Löwdin and Mulliken FCD values differ in sign or by more than a factor of 2.
Computes the state and transition charges without storing them when those blocks are not listed. No bare alias.

properties.name: Active one-particle density matrices
properties.brief: Active 1-RDMs of the adiabatic states (bra I) and diabatic 1-RDMs over the configurations.
properties.for: `SSR 1-RDM ACTIVE STATE=<k>`: k below the number of stored states
properties.variables: `SSR 1-RDM ACTIVE STATE=<k> K=<e>`, `SSR 1-RDM ADIABATIC K=<e>` (row I·m + J, column p·N + q), `SSR 1-RDM DIABATIC SPARSE K=<e>`
properties.files: cube files via `psi4.cubeprop(wfn)` with `CUBEPROP_TASKS` `SSR_DENSITIES` (`SSR_D_<label>_cassette<e>.cube`), `SSR_DIFFERENCE_DENSITIES` (`SSR_DD_<label>-<label 0>_cassette<e>.cube`), `SSR_TRANSITION_DENSITIES` (`SSR_TD_<label I>-<label J>_cassette<e>.cube`)
bullets: `REKS_REPORT_LEVEL` 5 dumps ρ^{(k)} and the diabatic blocks as `[DEBUG]` text.

properties.name: Relaxed dipole, quadrupole and atomic charges
properties.brief: Dipole, quadrupole (full Cartesian tensor and traceless part) and Mulliken and Löwdin charges of the relaxed density P^{r} of the CP-REKS (Z-vector) response of a state (§2).
properties.for: `energy()` and `gradient()`; one CP-REKS solve shared with the gradient and NAC targets
properties.units: e a_{0} (dipole; printed also D); e a_{0}^{2} (quadrupole); e (charges)
properties.variables: `SSR ROOT <r> RELAXED DIPOLE CASSETTE <e>`, `SSR ROOT <r> RELAXED QUADRUPOLES CASSETTE <e>`, `SSR ROOT <r> RELAXED MULLIKEN CHARGES CASSETTE <e>`, `SSR ROOT <r> RELAXED LOWDIN CHARGES CASSETTE <e>`, `SSR ROOT <r> RELAXED DENSITY CASSETTE <e>` (AO); `CURRENT DIPOLE` = relaxed dipole of the followed root when it is listed, otherwise unset
bullets: The charges of each state sum to the molecular charge.
P^{r} is not N-representable; the EKT block prints the count of its negative natural occupations (§ekt-states).

properties.name: Bond indices of the relaxed density
properties.brief: Mayer and Wiberg–Löwdin indices of P^{r}.
properties.variables: `SSR ROOT <r> RELAXED MAYER INDICES CASSETTE <e>`, `SSR ROOT <r> RELAXED WIBERG LOWDIN INDICES CASSETTE <e>` (natom × natom)
bullets: Not printed because P^{r} is not the density of a wavefunction.

properties.name: EKT ionization energies, pole strengths and Dyson orbitals of SI states
properties.brief: Extended Koopmans' theorem on the relaxed energy-weighted density W and the relaxed density P^{r} of a state: IP, ε, pole strength per spin orbital, Dyson orbitals; ref = lowest state of the first typed SI cassette (S0 for a singlet cassette).
properties.for: natural orbitals of P^{r} with occupation above `REKS_EKT_OCC_TOL` (10^{-6})
formulas: \mathbf W\mathbf c_k = \varepsilon_k\,\mathbf P\mathbf c_k, \qquad \mathbf c_k^{\mathsf T}\mathbf P\mathbf c_k = 1, \qquad \mathrm{IP}_k = -\varepsilon_k

\mathbf d_k = \mathbf P\mathbf c_k, \qquad \phi^{\mathrm{Dyson}}_k = \mathbf d_k/\sqrt2, \qquad \mathrm{pole}_k = \tfrac12|\mathbf d_k|^2, \qquad \sum_k \mathrm{pole}_k = \tfrac12\sum_{a\,\mathrm{kept}} p_a
properties.variables: `SSR EKT IONIZATION ENERGIES ROOT <r> CASSETTE <e>`, `SSR EKT POLE STRENGTHS ROOT <r> CASSETTE <e>`, `SSR EKT NATURAL OCCUPATIONS ROOT <r> CASSETTE <e>`, `SSR DYSON ORBITALS MO ROOT <r> CASSETTE <e>`, `SSR DYSON ORBITALS AO ROOT <r> CASSETTE <e>`
bullets: W is the symmetrized energy-weighted density of the state's response, P = P^{r} in the MO basis. The problem is solved in the natural orbitals of P with occupations p_{a} above `REKS_EKT_OCC_TOL`; smaller and negative ones are dropped.
States of a 2S > 0 cassette: spin-averaged EKT (spin-summed P^{r}).
One table per state at `REKS_REPORT_LEVEL` 2; level 3 adds the dropped eigenvalues and the Dyson MO block.

Check `sum of strengths` against half the sum of the occupations, the count of negative natural occupations of P^{r}, and the `Flag` column; strengths lie outside 0..1 by up to the lowest negative occupation.
properties.ref: Filatov et al., J. Chem. Theory Comput. 2020, 16, 4489.

properties.name: EKT ionization energies of the SA-REKS ensemble
properties.brief: Extended Koopmans' theorem on the generalized Fock matrix W and the fractional-occupation density D of the SA-REKS ensemble, in the block `==> Ionization energies (EKT) and Dyson orbitals, SA-REKS ensemble <==`.
properties.on: `REKS_EKT` true and no state listed in `SI_REKS_PROPERTY_FOR`
properties.for: the SCF finalize of `energy()` and `gradient()`
properties.variables: `REKS EKT IONIZATION ENERGIES`, `REKS EKT POLE STRENGTHS`, `REKS EKT NATURAL OCCUPATIONS`, `REKS DYSON ORBITALS MO`, `REKS DYSON ORBITALS AO` (sector form `REKS SECTOR <s> EKT ...` when the SA ensemble lies in run sector s above 0)
bullets: The equations of §ekt-states with W the symmetrized generalized Fock matrix and P = diag(2f), f = 1 (core), n/2 (active), 0 (virtual).
The `State analysis` line of `REKS_EKT` then names the SA-REKS ensemble.

properties.name: Nuclear gradients of SSR states
properties.brief: Gradient of an adiabatic SSR state from the CP-REKS response.
properties.for: `gradient()`; roots of `SI_REKS_NAC` pairs join the targets without being listed
properties.variables: `SSR ROOT <r> GRADIENT CASSETTE <e>`; `CURRENT ENERGY` and `REKS TARGET STATE ENERGY` (followed root, set in `energy()` too); `CURRENT GRADIENT`, `SCF TOTAL GRADIENT` (followed root)
bullets: The followed state (`*`) and `CURRENT ENERGY`: §si_reks_grad.
A root within `REKS_GRAD_DEGEN_TOL` (10^{-6} E_{h}) of another physical root of its cassette is computed with a warning. A meta-GGA functional raises an error: no analytic SI gradient.
`E` of a `Gradient of` block equals the state's energy in `Adiabatic states`; `Returned gradient` names the `*` state and repeats its table.
Converged response: `Remain` reaches 0 in the CP-REKS solver block (§reks_cpreks_conv); each gradient prints `|sum over atoms|` near zero.

properties.name: Nuclear gradient of the SA-REKS ensemble
properties.brief: Gradient of E_{SA}, returned by `gradient()` when no SI root is ordered; blocks `SA-REKS analytic gradient: targets`, `Gradient of the SA-REKS ensemble`, `Returned gradient`.
properties.variables: `CURRENT GRADIENT`, `SCF TOTAL GRADIENT` (stock psi4 names)
bullets: `CURRENT DIPOLE` is unset.

properties.name: Nonadiabatic coupling vectors
properties.brief: Derivative coupling between two adiabatic states of one cassette: a model part from the SI matrices and a residual part, the derivative of the configuration functions (orbital and FON response).
properties.for: `gradient()`
formulas: \mathbf d_{IJ} = \langle I|\tfrac{\mathrm d}{\mathrm d\mathbf R} J\rangle = \mathbf d_{\mathrm{model}} + \mathbf d_{\mathrm{residual}}, \qquad \mathbf d_{JI} = -\mathbf d_{IJ}
\mathbf d_{\mathrm{model}} = \frac{\mathbf c_I^{\mathsf T}\big(\mathrm d\mathbf H/\mathrm d\mathbf R - E_J\,\mathrm d\mathbf S/\mathrm d\mathbf R\big)\,\mathbf c_J}{E_J - E_I}
properties.variables: `SSR NAC <I> <J> CASSETTE <e>`, `SSR NAC MODEL <I> <J> CASSETTE <e>`, `SSR NAC RESIDUAL <I> <J> CASSETTE <e>`; the root gradients `SSR ROOT <I> GRADIENT CASSETTE <e>`, `SSR ROOT <J> GRADIENT CASSETTE <e>`
bullets: The sum rule is checked against −p from the velocity moments only when `SI_REKS_ANALYSIS` computes them (`E_TDM_VEL` or `M_TDM`); the line ends with `consistent` when the deviation is ≤ 10^{-6}, otherwise it reads `deviation …` without `consistent`. Without the moments the legend prints `-p_12 requires SI_REKS_ANALYSIS E_TDM_VEL`.
The header prints the gap of the pair (§diag-quasi-degenerate).

properties.name: Conical-intersection topography
properties.brief: Topography of the intersection of the pair A, B (lower, upper root) from the pair gradients G and the NAC: g̃, h̃ rotated by φ to mutual orthogonality, tilt s along them, pitch δ_{gh}, asymmetry Δ_{gh}, relative tilt σ, tilt heading θ_{s}, P (below 1 peaked, above 1 sloped), B (below 1 bifurcating, above 1 single path).
properties.for: every NAC pair (both root gradients are computed); table when E_{B} − E_{A} ≤ `REKS_CI_TOPOGRAPHY_GAP` (default 5·10^{-3} E_{h}), one line otherwise; variables at any gap
properties.units: E_{h}/a_{0} (|g̃|, |h̃|, s_{x}, s_{y}, δ_{gh}); rad (φ, θ_{s}); dimensionless (Δ_{gh}, σ, P, B); E_{h} (E_{B} − E_{A})
formulas: \mathbf g = \tfrac12(\mathbf G_B - \mathbf G_A), \qquad \mathbf h = (E_B - E_A)\,\mathbf d_{AB}, \qquad \mathbf s = \tfrac12(\mathbf G_A + \mathbf G_B)

\phi = \tfrac12\,\mathrm{atan2}(2\,\mathbf g\cdot\mathbf h,\ \mathbf g\cdot\mathbf g - \mathbf h\cdot\mathbf h), \qquad \tilde{\mathbf g} = \cos\phi\,\mathbf g + \sin\phi\,\mathbf h, \qquad \tilde{\mathbf h} = -\sin\phi\,\mathbf g + \cos\phi\,\mathbf h
s_x = \frac{\mathbf s\cdot\tilde{\mathbf g}}{|\tilde{\mathbf g}|}, \qquad s_y = \frac{\mathbf s\cdot\tilde{\mathbf h}}{|\tilde{\mathbf h}|}

\delta_{gh} = \sqrt{\tfrac12\big(|\tilde{\mathbf g}|^2 + |\tilde{\mathbf h}|^2\big)}, \qquad \Delta_{gh} = \frac{|\tilde{\mathbf g}|^2 - |\tilde{\mathbf h}|^2}{|\tilde{\mathbf g}|^2 + |\tilde{\mathbf h}|^2}
bullets: A is the lower root; d_{AB} is the full NAC (model + residual). The branch of φ gives |g̃| ≥ |h̃|, so Δ_{gh} ∈ [0, 1] and θ_{s} ∈ [0, π/2]. P is infinite when |h̃| vanishes, B when Δ_{gh} vanishes.
properties.variables: `SSR CI TOPOGRAPHY <I> <J> CASSETTE <e>` (1 × 12: |g̃|, |h̃|, φ, s_{x}, s_{y}, δ_{gh}, Δ_{gh}, σ, θ_{s}, P, B, E_{B} − E_{A}), `SSR CI G <I> <J> CASSETTE <e>`, `SSR CI H <I> <J> CASSETTE <e>`

properties.name: Spin-state gaps and Heisenberg J
properties.brief: Lowest state of each multiplicity over all cassettes, the gap between manifolds whose 2S differ by 2, the coupling J and the SI lowering of each state.
properties.on: SI cassettes on at least 2 spin manifolds
properties.for: manifolds with a physical root (a manifold declared by an empty block has none); J and its variables: manifolds whose 2S differ by 2
properties.units: E_{h} (stored J); printed E_{h}, eV and cm^{-1}
formulas: \mathrm{Gap} = E(\text{high spin}) - E(\text{low spin}), \qquad J = -\frac{\mathrm{Gap}}{2S_{\mathrm{high}}} \quad \text{for} \quad \hat H = -2J\,\hat{\mathbf S}_A\cdot\hat{\mathbf S}_B
properties.variables: `REKS HEISENBERG J`, `REKS HEISENBERG J SPINS` (rows [2S_lo, 2S_hi])
bullets: With three or more manifolds the block prints the ratio J(T/Q)/J(S/T); ratio 1 = one J for all spin pairs (Landé interval rule).
J is a spin-coupling constant only if the two states have the same open-shell orbitals and similar SI lowering (`Lowering(lo)`, `Lowering(hi)`).
